payload.feature:
FINISH ISSUE #1167: a cell that fits its column is never cut, and the cells a cut reports are the width of the text it returns, so the next column never shifts, in a walk that stays linear.

Read issue #1167 first. The branch is story-1167d-graph-fit, checked out in this worktree at dbbdf117. That is main 5c0386f13 plus nine commits from three earlier rounds:
- f026a03c, 024d77cf and 182a2eda (round one);
- 4cfb334a, a500ef63 and 361c7cdc (round two);
- 586fe01d, 8e134af1 and dbbdf117 (round three).

Read them first: `git log -p 5c0386f13..HEAD`. Rounds one, two and three stand. This round closes round three's one review finding and nothing else.

When you are done, the branch is dbbdf117 plus your commits. Do not rebase, squash, amend or merge main: the controller restacks. Where a choice is left open below, implement the option marked recommended, keep it small, and say which you took in your notes.

WHY ROUND THREE STOPPED. REVIEW-REFORGE-EXHAUSTED-MEDIUM on dbbdf117, with no security residual. Both members raised the same finding, and the chief confirmed it:
- **MEDIUM (W3; decision 0071 rulings 4 and 9).** crates/brokkr-cli/src/render/table.rs, near 180–194: `fit_by` assumes that appending a grapheme can only increase the display width.
  - In the locked unicode-width 0.2.2, Tifinagh `ⵏ⵿` (U+2D4F U+2D7F) measures two cells alone, and `ⵏ⵿ⴾ` (with U+2D3E) measures one: the joiner joins the pair.
  - **Symptom one:** in an eight-cell STATE column, `abcdefgⵏ⵿ⴾ` measures eight cells and fits. But `fit_by` returns `abcdefg…` as soon as the intermediate prefix reaches nine.
  - **Symptom two:** where there is room to finish, `saturating_sub` discards the one-cell decrease. The returned `cells` is then one too many, so the next column (ENTERED) is padded one cell to the left.
  - Reproduced by the adversarial member with the built CLI at COLUMNS=53 and COLUMNS=80, using two runs that entered `abcdefghi` and `abcdefgⵏ⵿ⴾ`.

THE CONTROLLER'S RULINGS (2026-11-20, under the standing ruling of 2026-11-04, "go with recommended"):
- **X1: a cell that fits is never cut.** A text whose whole width (`measure(text)`, measured once) is at most `max` comes back whole, and its `cells` is that whole width.
- **X2: the cells reported are measured, never summed.** Where a cut is made, `cells` is `measure(kept) + measure("…")`, both measured once on the final text. So the padding always matches what is printed, whatever the walk's approximation.
  - The walk's per-grapheme cost is signed: a decrease counts, and no `saturating_sub` hides it.
  - Recommended: measure the whole text once (X1). Only if it does not fit, walk once, choosing the cut by the signed pairwise sum as now, then measure the kept text once (X2).
  - That bounds the work at the walk's pairwise measurements plus two whole measurements per cell: still linear, and no prefix is remeasured.
- **X3: the linear bound stays bound.** Round three's counting test (measurements linear in the input) still passes. Extend it to count the extra whole measurements.
- **X4: everything else stands.**
  - W1 to W4 and their tests still hold; so do round one's and round two's rulings (M1 to M3, L1, L2).
  - NO_COLOR, `--json`, the empty-table header and the seats bytes stay pinned.
  - No golden is expected to move; name any that does. Public API: no change expected; say so.

TESTS (each named, each failing before your change):
- `abcdefgⵏ⵿ⴾ` in an eight-cell column comes back intact, with eight cells.
- Two rows whose STATE cells are `abcdefghi` and `abcdefgⵏ⵿ⴾ`, at a width with room for both: the next column starts at the same cell in both rows.
- A cut whose kept prefix ends just before a width decrease: the reported `cells` equals `measure` of the printed text.
- The counting test: measurements stay linear in the input, whole measurements included.
- Round one's, two's and three's tests all still pass.

THE JOURNAL RULE. Main is queue storage v6 or later. A brokkr built from this tree migrates any journal it opens for writing, and the lanes' pinned engines cannot read a migrated journal. Never run a brokkr built from this tree against a journal outside a test's own temporary directory.

THE EXACT COVERAGE GATE counts every line, branch and function of production code at 100%, closures included. Test files are excluded. Give each new arm a test.

GATES:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --locked -- --test-threads=16 graph render seats (timeout 280)
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- --test-threads=16 graph seats doc_truth doc_samples (timeout 280)
- cargo test -p brokkr-view --lib --locked -- --test-threads=16 graph (timeout 280)
- typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones, api and crap; git diff --check
- **TMPDIR** stays OUTSIDE this worktree (use /var/tmp, created in the same command if missing). Before reporting, `git status --short` shows no untracked file.
- **Test threads:** pass `--test-threads=16` to every cargo test you run by hand (#857).
- **Foreground only.** Run every command in the foreground and wait for it. Never end your turn with a background job pending.
- **The workspace tool.** A seat whose commands run through the `workspace` tool has a 300-second response limit per call. Wrap every command in `timeout 280` there. A gate that still cannot finish is reported UNVERIFIED, not retried. Write your result file before any optional extra check.

which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

result.notes: Answers round three's W3 MEDIUM with the recommended shape. fit_by measures the whole text once and returns it whole at that width when it fits (X1). Otherwise a new private kept_by walks once with a signed per-grapheme cost (measure(prev+g) - measure(prev) as isize; no saturating_sub) and stops at the first grapheme past the budget. The cells reported are then measure(kept) + measure("…"), measured once on the printed text (X2). Sizing with usize::MAX is now one whole measure per cell. Assumption: the walk stops at the first prefix past the budget, not at max as before; since the whole text is known not to fit, that is the cheapest linear cut. Tests, all in crates/brokkr-cli/src/render/tests.rs. Three are new: a_cell_that_fits_is_never_cut_where_its_width_falls, the_next_column_starts_where_it_does_after_a_width_that_falls and a_cut_reports_the_cells_of_the_text_it_prints. The last pins one cut that keeps the falling width and one that stops just before it, then loops over every max asserting cells == width_of(printed). Two are recounted (X3): a_cell_is_cut_in_one_walk_however_many_marks_it_carries goes from 3014 to 5022 (1008 whole + 3010 walk + 1004 kept and ellipsis), and a_row_is_padded_by_the_cells_its_cut_returned goes from 385 to 282. With dbbdf117's table.rs swapped back in, all five failed (.forge/t2.log): ('abcdefg…',8); the padding one cell short; ('abⵏ⵿ⴾcde…',8) where the text is 7 cells; 3014; 385. Mutations of the new code: reporting max(cells,max) failed a_cut_reports_the_cells_of_the_text_it_prints and a_cell_is_cut_and_padded_by_its_graphemes_widths (t3.log). Flooring each cost at 0 failed a_cut_reports_the_cells_of_the_text_it_prints (t4.log). Both mutations were restored. Gates passed: fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, brokkr-cli lib graph/render/seats (132 passed), brokkr-cli it graph/seats/doc_truth/doc_samples (53 passed), brokkr-view lib graph (21 passed), typos --hidden, git diff --check, ratchet files/clones/api, and the recipes/self compile. All test runs used TMPDIR=/var/tmp via cargo --config. PENDING: ratchet crap and the exact-coverage gate need scripts/coverage-exact.sh outside the box ('no LCOV at target/coverage/lcov.info'); every new branch (fits/cut, break/continue) is reached by the tests above. No golden moved. Public API unchanged (ratchet api holds); kept_by is private. Principle bent: the house uses `as isize` casts elsewhere (tui/movement.rs), and so does kept_by; a width over isize::MAX cannot occur. Possible follow-up, not fixed: when the signed walk underestimates a text whose whole width does not fit, the kept text can measure more than max-1. The cells are still measured, so the padding matches what is printed, but the column overflows by that excess.

result.notes: MEDIUM — correctness and adversarial, one alignment defect (X2/X4, W3, decision 0071 rulings 4 and 9). At 320f6ef5, crates/brokkr-cli/src/render/table.rs:203 counts the width reduction from overlapping Tifinagh joins twice. In an eight-cell STATE column, abcdⵏ⵿ⴾ⵿ⵏefXYZ is cut to abcdⵏ⵿ⴾ⵿ⵏef…, ten cells. Line 179 measures those ten cells correctly, and line 229 pads by zero, shifting ENTERED two cells right relative to abcdefgh. Ensure the measured cut including the ellipsis fits the column in linear work, and assert both the width bound and alignment for overlapping joins. The recommended whole-width check preserves fitting cells, and the counting test includes the whole measurements. No golden or public API changed. Reviewed the supplied issue framing and commit history. Exact coverage was not independently verified.

Answers the review finding on 320f6ef5 (overlapping Tifinagh joins: the walk's signed pairwise sum counts each pair's fall, so abcdⵏ⵿ⴾ⵿ⵏefXYZ cut at 8 kept 10 cells and ENTERED shifted). Commit 0469ab0f on top of 320f6ef5, which is the head this round was handed. The framing names dbbdf117 as the base, but the run context shows review at 320f6ef5, and that commit already holds X1 and X2. Change in crates/brokkr-cli/src/render/table.rs: kept_by now returns where each kept grapheme ends, with a leading 0. A new fitting() measures the walk's cut, and while that cut passes the budget it halves the kept grapheme count, down to none, which measures 0 and always fits. The work stays linear: the whole text, plus the walk, plus at most 2x the kept text. A text that fits is still returned whole (X1). The cells reported are still measure(kept) + measure("…") (X2). Trade-off I chose (smallest linear option): in pathological overlapping-join text the halving can drop more than needed. abcdⵏ⵿ⴾ⵿ⵏefXYZ at 8 prints abcd… (5 cells). It still fits and stays aligned. A tighter cut would need a non-linear back-off; stepping back one grapheme at a time gives a better cut but measured 43414 scalars against 2407. New tests in render/tests.rs: (1) a_cut_where_joins_overlap_fits_its_column: for every max it asserts cells == width_of(printed) and cells <= max; it also checks a 16-wide STATE/ENTERED table where the abcdefghij row and the joined-name row put ENTERED in the same column. (2) a_cut_where_joins_overlap_is_made_in_linear_work: 200 ⵏ⵿ joins cut at 8 measure exactly 2407 scalars, broken down in the test comment.
